subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack message_changed/message_deleted events remain session-scoped system events, or should OpenClaw add an opt-in channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes suppression field for them?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the requested fix creates a new public Slack config surface and changes event-context policy, which repository policy treats as maintainer/product territory rather than an automatic bug lane.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
options.body: Add ignoreSubtypes as a documented Slack plugin config field, default to current behavior, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context.

options.title: Change default policy
options.body: Stop queuing edit/delete system events by default and accept the compatibility impact for users who currently consume those metadata events as passive context.

options.title: Keep current system events
options.body: Decline the config key and keep edit/delete metadata flowing into session-scoped system events, with docs clarifying the intended behavior or workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
recommendation.body: Add ignoreSubtypes as a documented Slack plugin config field, default to current behavior, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on Slack subtype policy and the adjacent thread_broadcast decision.
